key_findings: Both groups performed exceptionally well, scoring 98% (Group A: 196/200) and 97% (Group B: 194/200) respectively — a difference of only 2 points.

Group A's edge comes from: (1) Q9: mentioning Azure Managed Redis (port 10000, RedisCluster with SSL) and DEGRADED health status that Group B missed; (2) Q15: mentioning the 20-item-per-collection limit in add_item that Group B omitted.

Both groups lost points on Q4 (both incorrectly claimed user.py API needs GET endpoint changes when ground truth says no changes needed) and Q8 (both missed drop_tables() DELETE-not-DROP behavior and shared Base declarative_base).
Both groups missed imgproxy thumbnail generation and medium-URL fallback detail in Q14 (smart image management).
Both groups demonstrated deep knowledge of the codebase with accurate file paths, function names, and data flow descriptions across auth-service and product-service.
The answers are remarkably similar in quality — the 2-point gap is marginal and reflects minor completeness differences rather than any correctness issues.
Auth-service questions (Q1-Q10): Group A scored 97/100 vs Group B 96/100. Product-service questions (Q11-Q20): Group A scored 99/100 vs Group B 98/100.
Both groups excelled at: cross-provider linking logic, JWT cache mechanisms, cache invalidation strategies, three-phase DB patterns, and circular navigation algorithms.
